sections.h2: Where do Walton County owners deal with property taxes?
sections.html:
Walton County owners work with the tax collector, who bills and collects, and the property appraiser, who sets values and exemptions. The tax collector's office runs three branches: the DeFuniak Springs courthouse for north Walton, the Santa Rosa Beach courthouse annex for south Walton, and a Freeport office. The mailing address is a post office box in DeFuniak Springs.

The collector's site shows the branches open on weekdays into late afternoon, with a slightly later Wednesday start. Property tax questions about the estimated tax on a TRIM notice go to the property appraiser, while payment and delinquency questions go to the collector's office.

Because the county stretches from the Gulf coast to the inland towns, a seller may live a long way from the office that holds the file. Online payment and the parcel search save the trip.

sections.h2: What is the Walton County property tax calendar?
sections.html:
The tax collector publishes a month by month list, and it is more detailed than most Florida counties. Here are the entries that matter to a home seller.

Walton County Tax Collector calendar for real estate taxes
MonthEntry on the collector's page
January2% discount
February1% discount
MarchExemptions due to the Property Appraiser by March 1; full amount due by March 31; fourth installment due March 31
AprilUnpaid real estate tax delinquent April 1 with a 3% charge; installment plan applications for next year due April 30
MayDelinquent real estate taxes advertised once a week for three weeks; certificate sale on or before June 1
June to SeptemberFirst installment due June 30, second due September 30
NovemberBills mailed; 4% discount through November 30
December3% discount; third installment due December 31

Source: Walton County Tax Collector, important tax dates. The page also notes the property appraiser mails the TRIM notice in August.

sections.h2: How does the Walton County installment plan work?
sections.html:
The plan splits the year into four payments, with a discount on the first three. The tax collector's installment page and calendar describe it this way.

  • Applications for the following year are due April 30.
  • The prior year's tax must exceed $100.00 and not be paid through escrow.
  • June 30 brings the first installment, carrying a 6% discount, September 30 the second at 4.5%, the third December 31 with 3%, and the fourth March 31 with no discount.
  • The first two payments are each one quarter of the previous year's taxes.
  • If the first payment is missed, the owner is out of the plan for the year. The calendar says the first installment must be received by July 31 or participation ends.

Enrolled taxpayers do not need to reapply each year. A seller on the plan should ask the collector for the balance left after each payment, since the later installments are adjusted after the roll is set.

sections.h2: What happens when Walton County taxes become delinquent?
sections.html:
On April 1 unpaid real estate tax is delinquent and a 3% charge is added to the gross amount. Tangible personal property tax is different: it picks up 1.5% interest per month.

The collector then runs the delinquent list in the DeFuniak Herald for three straight weeks, and the advertising and auction fee is added to the bill. The certificate sale follows, scheduled by June 1 as an online auction at lienhub.com/county/walton. Bidding starts at 18% and drops in quarter-percent steps, with a 5% minimum interest unless the bid is zero. A certificate is good for seven years.

Once the holder has waited two years from the April 1 delinquency date, an application for a tax deed is possible. The collector states that tax deed sales are set by the Clerk of Court and run online at walton.realforeclose.com, and that the owner may redeem until the clerk signs the tax deed. Delinquent taxes can be paid by cash, cashier's check, money order or card, with a convenience fee on card payments.

sections.h2: How do exemptions and the March 1 date affect a Walton County seller?
sections.html:
Exemptions follow the owner, so a sale ends the seller's homestead and the buyer must file their own. The tax collector's calendar sets the filing date at March 1 with the property appraiser, the same date the state taxpayer guide gives (link).

The state homestead exemption is up to $50,000, the first $25,000 for all taxes and an additional amount for non-school taxes on value above $50,000, according to the state homestead guide. Owners lose homestead if they rent the property or stop living there.

The tax collector also has a page on military property taxes. Servicemembers who rent a homestead out are covered by a separate state provision, so ask the collector if that applies.

sections.h2: Who pays the taxes when a Walton County home sells?
sections.html:
The contract decides, and closings in Florida normally prorate taxes to the day of closing. The title agent asks the collector for the current balance, including any certificate, and pays it from the seller's side of the statement.

The clerk collects deed stamps at filing, at 70 cents on each $100 of price, and every party to the document is liable whoever agrees to pay, per the stamp tax page. Clerk filing charges come from s. 28.24, which starts at $5.00 for a first page and adds $4.00 per further page, with extra per-page charges.

For a house with a tax certificate, the redemption has to be paid before or at closing. A buyer who sees a certificate issued more than two years ago should ask the Clerk of Court whether a tax deed application is pending.

sections.h2: How should a Walton County owner with unpaid taxes plan a sale?
sections.html:
Contact the tax collector first, because each month moves the cost. A sale before April avoids the 3% charge and the advertising fee, while one after the certificate sale carries interest and fees.

  • Search the parcel on the tax collector's payment portal for the current balance.
  • Ask whether a certificate exists and what rate it sold at.
  • Check homestead status with the property appraiser before March 1.
  • Tell the title company so the payoff is ordered ahead of the closing date.

sections.h2: How are Walton County tangible personal property taxes treated?
sections.html:
Tax on business equipment follows a harsher track than real estate. The tax collector's calendar says unpaid tangible personal property tax is delinquent April 1 and picks up 1.5% interest for each month.

Within 45 days after the March 31 deadline, those delinquent accounts are advertised in a local newspaper at the owner's cost. A list is published once in May, and warrant processing begins June 1. A landlord or small business owner selling a rental with equipment inside should ask the collector whether a personal property account sits under the same owner name.

  • Discounts match real estate: 4% in November, 3% in December, 2% in January, 1% in February.
  • Delinquent real estate carries a flat 3% charge, not monthly interest.
  • Different advertising rules apply to each, so ask which list a parcel is on.

sections.h2: What does a Walton County tax certificate holder have to wait for?
sections.html:
The holder cannot move fast. A certificate on a Walton County parcel is valid for seven years, and the holder may apply for a tax deed only two years after the April 1 delinquency date. Under state law the holder also may not contact the owner to demand payment during the first two years, per the statute on certificate sales.

For the seller, that window is time to arrange a sale. Many owners use it to list the house, find a buyer, and let the closing agent redeem the certificate from proceeds. Ask the collector for the redemption total on the planned closing date, because interest runs by the month.

faqs.q: When do Walton County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. The Walton County Tax Collector says unpaid real estate tax is delinquent on that date and a 3% charge is added to the gross amount.

faqs.q: What is the Walton County installment plan discount?
faqs.a: 6% on the first installment, 4.5% on the second, 3% on the third and none on the fourth. Applications are due April 30.

faqs.q: Where does Walton County hold its tax certificate sale?
faqs.a: Online, at lienhub.com/county/walton, on or before June 1. Bidding starts at 18% and goes down in quarter-percent steps.

faqs.q: Can I still keep my house after a Walton County tax certificate is sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The owner may redeem until the Clerk of Court signs the tax deed. A tax deed application cannot be filed until two years after the April 1 delinquency date.

faqs.q: When is the Walton County exemption deadline?
faqs.a: March 1. The tax collector's calendar says exemptions are due to the Property Appraiser's Office by that date.
